base_candidate.role: frozen detector, execution semantics, leadership, portfolio arbitration and Nautilus account path

hypothesis.problem: Candidate 13 retained strong but sparse opportunities; Candidate 14 increased opportunity density but aliased failed auctions and true acceptance, producing a 20% win rate over the 2026-05-11 through 2026-08-03 continuous account path.
hypothesis.causal_claim: After external liquidity is traded through, the conversion of aggressive flow into price progress, unexplained impact and occupancy beyond the boundary distinguishes swept-side acceptance from absorbed or reclaimed flow before inherited FAR/AAC confirmation.
hypothesis.router: FAILURE admits inherited FAR; ACCEPTANCE admits inherited AAC; UNRESOLVED is no trade.
hypothesis.non_goal: The router does not fit future return, alter targets, change risk, add leverage caps or replace NautilusTrader.

router.calibration: up to 120 completed pre-sweep one-minute bars
router.impact_model: non-negative contemporaneous log-return response to signed aggressor-flow pressure weighted by square-root relative volume
channels: close occupancy beyond the latest crossed external boundary
router.sequential_rule: bounded channel mean accumulates log(2) units at full agreement; symmetric boundary log(9) corresponds to a 10% design error budget but is an evidence convention, not a calibrated posterior probability
router.reset: a new sweep extreme or crossed boundary starts a new causal episode

selection.method: Intervals were committed before Candidate 15 outcomes. D1 intentionally replays a known Candidate 14 loss cluster for mechanism diagnosis. H1 is an ordinary-regime confirmation interval outside Candidate 14 L1. S1 is a separately predeclared liquidation-stress interval. H1/S1 are Candidate-15-unseen but are not represented as project-wide untouched data.

evaluation.interpretation: Three isolated weeks are screening and mechanism evidence. They cannot by themselves establish long-run success.

research_basis.source: Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov, The Price Impact of Order Book Events, arXiv:1011.6402
research_basis.use: price response is evaluated against order-flow imbalance rather than volume alone

research_basis.source: Adams and MacKay, Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection, arXiv:0710.3742
research_basis.use: latest causal run resets when a new sweep extreme changes the episode

research_basis.source: Abhishek and Mannor, A nonparametric sequential test for online randomized experiments, arXiv:1610.02490
research_basis.use: continuous monitoring requires an explicit sequential stopping boundary

research_basis.source: Hu and Zhang, Stochastic Price Dynamics in Response to Order Flow Imbalance, arXiv:2505.17388
research_basis.use: response horizon and regime dependence motivate UNRESOLVED rather than a universal static label
